repo.name: FlashShot-Screen-Capture
repo.description: Capture part of your Windows screen in a keystroke: drag a region, annotate it with arrows, text, numbers and censor boxes, then copy or save. Tray app, offline, no dependencies.

releases.body_html:
First release of FlashShot Screen Capture 📸

  • ⌨️ One key from any app: Print Screen by default (change it in Settings), freezes every monitor and lets you drag a region
  • ✂️ Precise region: any drag direction, resize from corners and edges, move it with the arrow keys, live size in pixels, across monitors
  • ✏️ Annotations that stay editable: arrow, line, rectangle, ellipse, pen, marker, text, numbering and opaque censor boxes, with undo and redo
  • 📋 Copy (Ctrl+C) or Save as PNG or JPEG; Ctrl+S saves straight to the last folder, Ctrl+drag copies on release
  • 🔒 100% offline, no dependencies, ~0 CPU while waiting

Install: download FlashShotSetup.exe below and run it. Per-user install, no admin rights needed. Windows 10 (1809+) and 11, 64-bit.

apps.readmeHtml:
📸 FlashShot — Screen Capture

Press a key, drag over part of the screen, mark it up and copy or save it. ⚡
No editor window to open, no account, no upload: everything happens right on top of the frozen screen and stays on your PC.

🚀 Features

  • ⌨️ One shortcut from any app: Print Screen by default, change it in Settings
  • 🧊 Frozen screen: the desktop is captured first, so videos and animations stop while you select
  • 🖥️ Every monitor: selections can cross screens, also with monitors left of or above the main one and different scaling
  • ✂️ Precise region: drag in any direction, resize from the corners and edges, move it with the mouse or one pixel at a time with the arrow keys, live size in pixels
  • ✏️ Annotations that stay editable until you export: select, move, resize, recolor or delete any of them
    • ↗️ Arrow · ➖ Line · ▭ Rectangle · ◯ Ellipse (Shift for 45° steps, squares and circles)
    • 🖊️ Pen · 🖍️ Marker (see-through, never darker where it crosses itself)
    • 🔤 Text (multi-line, size, color, optional background) · 1️⃣ Numbering (1, 2, 3… per capture)
    • ⬛ Censor: an opaque box; the hidden pixels are not in the exported image at all
  • ↩️ Undo and redo for every drawing, move, resize, style change or text edit, numbers included
  • 📋 Copy (Ctrl+C) puts the image on the clipboard, ready to paste anywhere
  • 💾 Save as PNG or JPEG with the usual Windows dialog, or Ctrl+S to save straight to the last folder with a dated name
  • ⚡ Ctrl+drag copies the region the moment you release the mouse
  • 🎨 Remembers each tool's color and size
  • 🔒 100% offline: nothing leaves your PC. No telemetry, no accounts
  • 🌙 Windows 11 look that follows your light or dark theme and accent color
  • 🪶 Tiny: a ~0.4 MB program, no .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed, ~0 CPU while waiting
  • 🚦 Starts with Windows (you can turn it off)

📦 Install

Download FlashShotSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Per-user install, no admin rights needed
  • FlashShot opens a small window with New capture and Settings, then keeps running in the notification area
  • It starts with Windows from then on

💡 Print Screen busy? Windows 11 can use Print Screen for its Snipping Tool, and other capture apps take it too. FlashShot tells you when that happens: turn that option off in Windows Settings → Accessibility → Keyboard, close the other app, or pick another shortcut in FlashShot's Settings.

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes FlashShot, its startup entry and its settings.

🖱️ Usage

Action How
New capture Print Screen, the tray icon, or New capture in FlashShot's window
Select a region Drag anywhere; Esc closes the capture
Resize / move the region Drag its corners or edges / drag inside it with the Select tool, or use the arrow keys
Copy as soon as you release Hold Ctrl while dragging the region
Draw Pick a tool and drag inside the region
Edit an annotation Select tool (V): click it, drag it or its handles, change its color or size
Edit a text again Double-click it
Finish a text Click elsewhere or Ctrl+Enter (Esc cancels the edit)
Delete an annotation Select it and press Delete
Undo / redo Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z
Copy and close Ctrl+C or Copy
Save Save (choose where) or Ctrl+S (last folder, never overwrites)
Settings Tray icon → Settings, or the Settings button

⌨️ Tool keys

Key Tool Key Tool
V Select P Pen
A Arrow M Marker
L Line T Text
R Rectangle N Numbering
E Ellipse X Censor

Shapes and Draw are grouped on the toolbar: click the active group again to switch between its tools.

🔧 Build

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ x64 tools and Inno Setup 6 (winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup).

.\build.ps1

It downloads the pinned build tools into .deps/ (Windows SDK, CMake and Ninja, all verified by hash), builds everything, runs the tests and writes the installer to dist/FlashShotSetup.exe.

.\build.ps1 -SkipTests and .\build.ps1 -SkipInstaller skip those steps.

📚 Dependencies

None: FlashShot only uses Windows' own APIs (GDI and GDI+ for drawing, the Windows Imaging Component for PNG and JPEG, the standard clipboard and file dialogs). 🧘

🪟 Compatibility

Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer) and Windows 11, 64-bit.

releases.body_html:
Iris is now Iris Image, with a new minimalist logo.

Changes

  • New name: the context menu entry is now Iris Image — Convert to....
  • New, cleaner logo.
  • The installer is now IrisImageSetup.exe.

Installing over Iris 1.0.0 upgrades it in place; no need to uninstall first.

Download

  • IrisImageSetup.exe: installer. Requires administrator rights (needed for the Windows 11 context menu without a paid code-signing certificate). No other runtime or codec needs to be installed.

Requirements

Windows 10 version 1809 or later, or Windows 11 (x64).

First release of Iris, a tiny utility that converts images straight from the Windows File Explorer context menu.

Right-click one or more images, choose Iris — Convert to... and pick a format. The converted copy appears next to the original.

Download

  • IrisSetup.exe: installer. Requires administrator rights (needed for the Windows 11 context menu without a paid code-signing certificate). No other runtime or codec needs to be installed.

Highlights

  • Output formats: PNG, JPG, WebP, BMP, GIF, TIFF and ICO (multi-size).
  • Modern context menu on Windows 11, classic context menu on Windows 10.
  • Converts whole selections in one job; never modifies or overwrites files (photo (1).webp).
  • Keeps transparency, applies EXIF orientation and keeps RGB color profiles.
  • No background processes, no telemetry, works offline.

Requirements

Windows 10 version 1809 or later, or Windows 11 (x64).

Known limitations

  • Animated GIF/WebP and multi-page TIFF files: only the first frame is converted.
  • The Windows 11 menu package is registered for the account that approves the installer's administrator prompt.

apps.readmeHtml:
👁️ Iris Image — Instant Image Converter

Convert images straight from the Windows File Explorer context menu. 🖱️
Right-click an image, choose Iris Image — Convert to... and a format, and the converted copy appears next to the original. That's it.

No windows, no settings, no background processes. Iris Image only runs while it is converting, then exits.

🚀 Features

  • 🖼️ Converts to PNG, JPG, WebP, BMP, GIF, TIFF and ICO
  • 🪟 Native context menu: the modern menu on Windows 11, the classic menu on Windows 10
  • 📚 Converts a whole selection in one go, using up to four threads
  • 🛡️ Never modifies or overwrites anything: if photo.webp exists, you get photo (1).webp
  • 🧹 Never leaves half-written files behind, even if something fails
  • 🫥 Keeps transparency where the format supports it; JPG is flattened onto white
  • 📱 Applies EXIF orientation, so rotated phone photos stay upright
  • 🎨 Keeps embedded RGB color profiles (PNG, JPG, TIFF, WebP)
  • 🔌 Works offline. No telemetry, no updater, no services
  • 🪶 Tiny: a ~0.9 MB executable and a ~160 KB shell extension, no .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed

🖼️ Supported formats

Format Read Write Notes
PNG ✅ ✅ Keeps 16-bit and grayscale images as they are.
JPG ✅ ✅ Quality 90. Transparency is flattened onto white.
WebP ✅ ✅ Lossy, quality 90, with alpha. Max 16383 × 16383 pixels.
BMP ✅ ✅ 32-bit with alpha (BITMAPV5) when the image has transparency.
GIF ✅ ✅ 256-color palette with dithering and transparency.
TIFF ✅ ✅ Lossless ZIP compression.
ICO ✅ ✅ Multi-size icon: 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 px (never upscaled).

🎞️ Animations and multi-page files: Iris Image converts the first frame of animated GIF and WebP files and the first page of multi-page TIFF files. When reading an icon, it uses the largest image in it.

🔁 Same format: when every selected file already has the target format, that format is hidden from the submenu. In a mixed selection, files already in the target format are skipped instead of being recompressed.

📦 Install

Download IrisImageSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Asks for administrator rights once, to add Iris Image to the Windows 11 context menu (see below)

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes Iris Image and its context menu entries.

🔐 Why does it ask for administrator rights?

The Windows 11 context menu only shows entries from apps with a package identity. Iris Image gets one from a small package that contains no code. Windows only accepts such a package without a paid code-signing certificate when an administrator installs it.

On Windows 10, or if the package cannot be registered, Iris Image uses the classic context menu instead (on Windows 11 it then appears under Show more options).

🖱️ Usage

  1. Right-click one or more images in File Explorer.
  2. Choose Iris Image — Convert to... and pick a format.

The new files appear in the same folder. ✨
If something goes wrong (a damaged file, a read-only folder, a full disk), a single Windows notification explains it. Successful conversions show no message.

It can also be used from scripts:

Iris.exe convert <png|jpg|webp|bmp|gif|tiff|ico> <image>...

⚙️ How it works

Part Role
IrisShell.dll The Explorer menu (IExplorerCommand). It never opens images: it only starts Iris.exe with the selected files, so Explorer stays fast and safe.
Iris.exe Converts the images, shows a notification on errors and exits.
Iris.msix Small package that adds the menu to the Windows 11 context menu.

Images are handled by the Windows Imaging Component, which is part of Windows, except WebP, which uses libwebp. Each image is written to a hidden temporary file in the destination folder and renamed only when complete; the rename never replaces an existing file.

🔧 Build

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the Desktop development with C++ workload, and Inno Setup 6 (winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup).

.\build.ps1

It downloads pinned, hash-checked copies of the Windows SDK and libwebp into .deps/ if missing, builds everything, runs the tests and writes the installer to dist/IrisImageSetup.exe. Use -SkipTests or -SkipInstaller to shorten it.

🧪 To run the tests on their own:

.\build\IrisTests.exe .\build\Iris.exe

📁 Project layout:

src/core/     Conversion engine and safe file output
src/app/      Iris.exe (worker and notifications)
src/shell/    IrisShell.dll (Explorer menu)
package/      Package manifest for the Windows 11 menu
installer/    Inno Setup script
tests/        Automated tests

📚 Dependencies

  • Windows Imaging Component — reading and writing images, built into Windows
  • libwebp — WebP images

See third-party notices for licenses.

🪟 Compatibility

Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer) and Windows 11, 64-bit.

repo.name: Iro-Color-Picker
repo.description: Pick any color from anywhere on your Windows screen: tray app with a pixel-exact magnifier, HEX/RGB/HSL/HSV/CMYK and recent colors. Offline, no dependencies.

releases.body_html:
First release of Iro Color Picker 🎨

  • 💧 Pick a color anywhere on screen with Ctrl + Alt + C: a magnifier follows the pointer for pixel-exact picks (mouse wheel to zoom, arrow keys to move one pixel)
  • 🧾 Copies as HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, CMYK or plain R, G, B, your choice
  • 🕘 Recent colors in the tray menu and in the Colors window, with every format one click away
  • 🔒 100% offline, ~0.5 MB of memory while idle, no dependencies

Install: download IroSetup.exe below and run it. Per-user install, no admin rights needed. Windows 10 (1809+) and 11, 64-bit.

apps.readmeHtml:
🎨 Iro — Color Picker

Pick any color from anywhere on your screen. 💧
Press a shortcut, point at a pixel with the magnifier, click, and the color is on your clipboard: #1A73E8, rgb(26, 115, 232), hsl(…)… whatever you need.

Iro lives in the notification area, uses almost no memory and works offline, on your PC.

🚀 Features

  • 💧 Pick a color (Ctrl + Alt + C): a magnifier follows your pointer over a frozen copy of the screen, so you hit the exact pixel. Click and the color is copied
  • 🔍 Zoom in or out with the mouse wheel; move one pixel at a time with the arrow keys (ten with Shift)
  • 🧾 Several formats: HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, CMYK or plain R, G, B. Choose the one you copy by default, and the magnifier shows the color in it as you go
  • 🕘 Recent colors: your last 24 colors, in the tray menu and in the Colors window
  • 🖌️ Colors window: the selected color large, in every format with its own copy button
  • 🖱️ Left-click the tray icon to pick; right-click for the menu
  • 🔒 100% offline: nothing leaves your PC. No telemetry, no accounts
  • 🖥️ Multiple monitors, mixed DPI scaling and monitors placed left of or above the main one
  • 🌙 Clean Windows 11 look that follows your light or dark theme and accent color
  • 🪶 Tiny: ~0.5 MB of memory and 0% CPU while idle, a ~2.2 MB installer, no .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed
  • 🚦 Starts with Windows (you can turn it off)

📦 Install

Download IroSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Per-user install, no admin rights needed
  • Iro starts right away and its icon appears in the notification area
  • It starts with Windows from then on

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes Iro, its startup entry, its settings and its recent colors.

🖱️ Usage

Action How
Pick a color Ctrl + Alt + C, or left-click the tray icon, then click the pixel
Move one pixel Arrow keys (Shift + arrow: ten pixels), then Enter or Space to pick
Zoom the magnifier Mouse wheel
Cancel Esc or right-click
Copy a recent color again Right-click the tray icon and click the color
Change the copied format Right-click the tray icon → Copy as
All formats of a color Right-click the tray icon → Colors…
Settings Right-click the tray icon → Settings
Exit Right-click the tray icon → Exit Iro

After picking, a small note with the color sample (#1A73E8 copied) appears next to the pointer and fades away. Just paste with Ctrl + V.

In the Colors window, click a recent color to see it in every format, use the copy button next to the one you want, or double-click a color to copy its HEX value.

🧾 Formats

Format Example
HEX #1A73E8
RGB rgb(26, 115, 232)
HSL hsl(214, 82%, 51%)
HSV hsv(214, 89%, 91%)
CMYK cmyk(89%, 50%, 0%, 9%)
R, G, B 26, 115, 232

HEX, RGB and HSL paste straight into CSS. CMYK is the simple conversion design tools show, without a print color profile.

⚙️ Settings

  • Copy as: the format copied after picking
  • Recent colors: remember them or not, and clear them

repo.name: Kodo-QR-Instant
repo.description: Read and create QR codes on Windows in a second: tray app with a screen-region QR reader, clipboard-to-QR, Wi-Fi/contact/email templates and history. Offline.

releases.body_html:
Reading a QR code now feels like scanning one ✨

  • ✨ Scan effect: when Kodo reads a code on your screen, a light sweeps over it, the frame glows and a few sparks fly off
  • 🔊 A nicer sound: a soft glass chime replaces the old beep (you can still turn it off in Settings)
  • ⭐ Favorite links open by themselves: scan a link you've marked as a favorite and it opens right away

Install: download KodoSetup.exe below and run it; it upgrades your current Kodo and keeps your settings.

Kodo now reads QR codes with your camera too 📷

  • 📷 Read with the camera (Ctrl + Shift + Alt + Q): hold up a QR code on your phone, a ticket or a poster and it's read the moment it's in view. Choose the camera if you have several, and turn the mirror view on or off
  • ⚠️ Safer links: short links (bit.ly…), look-alike addresses, bare IPs and unencrypted links get a warning, and opening them asks first
  • ⭐ Favorites in the history: keep the codes you reuse (your Wi-Fi, your contact card) on top
  • 🔊 A short beep, and a green flash on the camera, when a code is read. You can turn the sound off in Settings

Install: download KodoSetup.exe below and run it; it upgrades your current Kodo and keeps your settings.

First release of Kodo QR Instant 🔳

  • 🔍 Read a QR code anywhere on screen with Ctrl + Shift + Q: links (open/copy), Wi-Fi (network and password), text (copied to the clipboard), email, phone, SMS, contacts and locations
  • ✨ Create a QR code from the clipboard with Ctrl + Shift + G, then copy it as an image or save it as PNG
  • 🧩 Templates for Wi-Fi, contacts (vCard) and email
  • 🕘 Local history, which you can turn off or clear
  • 🔒 100% offline, ~0.6 MB of memory while idle

Install: download KodoSetup.exe below and run it. Per-user install, no admin rights needed. Windows 10 (1809+) and 11, 64-bit.

apps.readmeHtml:
🔳 Kodo — QR Instant

Read and create QR codes on your PC in a second. ⚡
Press a shortcut, drag over a QR code anywhere on your screen, and see what's inside. Or turn your clipboard into a QR code, ready to scan with your phone.

Kodo lives in the notification area, uses almost no memory and works offline, on your PC.

  

🚀 Features

  • 🔍 Read a QR code (Ctrl + Shift + Q): select an area of the screen and a small card shows what the code holds
    • 🔗 Links: open them in your browser or copy them. Short links (bit.ly…), look-alike addresses, bare IPs and unencrypted links get a warning and ask before opening
    • 📶 Wi-Fi: see the network name and password, copy either one
    • 📋 Text: copied straight to your clipboard
    • 📧 Emails, 📞 phone numbers, 💬 text messages, 👤 contacts (vCard / MeCard) and 📍 locations too
    • Several codes in the selection? Go through them with Next code
  • 📷 Read with the camera (Ctrl + Shift + Alt + Q): a window opens your default camera; hold up a QR code (on your phone, a ticket, a poster…) and it's read the moment it's in view. Pick another camera if you have several, and turn the mirror view on or off
  • ✨ Create a QR code from the clipboard (Ctrl + Shift + G): copy any text or link, press the shortcut and the code is there
    • 🖼️ Copy image to paste it into a chat or a document, or 💾 Save PNG
  • 🧩 Templates: create codes for a 📶 Wi-Fi network, a 👤 contact (vCard) or an 📧 email, with a live preview
  • 🕘 History: the codes you read and create, to show them again or copy their text. Mark the ones you reuse (your Wi-Fi, your contact card) as ⭐ favorites to keep them on top. Scanning a favorite link opens it right away. Stays on your PC, and you can turn it off
  • ✨ A light sweeps over the code you selected, with a glow and a few sparks, and a soft glass sound plays (a green flash on the camera). You can turn the sound off
  • 🖱️ Left-click the tray icon to read a code; right-click for the menu
  • 🔒 100% offline: screenshots, camera images and codes never leave your PC. No telemetry, no accounts
  • 🌍 Accents, emoji and any alphabet (日本語, Русский…) both when reading and creating
  • 🌗 Reads dark-mode codes (light on dark), rotated and tiny on-screen codes
  • 🖥️ Multiple monitors, mixed DPI scaling and monitors placed left of or above the main one
  • 🌙 Clean Windows 11 look that follows your light or dark theme and accent color
  • 🪶 Tiny: ~0.6 MB of memory and 0% CPU while idle, a ~2.6 MB installer, no .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed
  • 🚦 Starts with Windows (you can turn it off)

📦 Install

Download KodoSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Per-user install, no admin rights needed
  • Kodo starts right away and its icon appears in the notification area
  • It starts with Windows from then on

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes Kodo, its startup entry, its settings and its history.

🖱️ Usage

Action How
Read a QR code Ctrl + Shift + Q, or left-click the tray icon, then drag over the code
Read with the camera Ctrl + Shift + Alt + Q, or right-click the tray icon → Read QR with camera
Create a QR from the clipboard Ctrl + Shift + G, or right-click the tray icon → Create QR from clipboard
Wi-Fi, contact or email code Right-click the tray icon → Create QR code… and pick a template
History Right-click the tray icon → History
Cancel a selection Esc or right-click
Settings Right-click the tray icon → Settings
Exit Right-click the tray icon → Exit Kodo

After reading, the card closes with Esc, the ✕ button or by clicking elsewhere. Enter runs the main action (e.g. Open link). If there's no QR code in the selection, Kodo tells you with a small No QR code found note.

🛡️ For your safety, Kodo only opens http and https links. Anything else (files, programs, other schemes) is shown as text, never run.

⚙️ Settings

  • Shortcuts for reading and creating
  • History: keep it or not, and clear it (favorites are kept)
  • Sound when a code is read
  • Start with Windows

🎯 What it reads

All QR code variants: QR Code, Micro QR and rMQR, as they appear on screen: in web pages, PDFs, images, videos or a video call.

Tip: select the code with a little space around it. Very small codes (2 pixels per module) are read too, but zooming in helps if a code is blurry.

Codes Kodo creates use the standard error correction level M (15%) and fit up to ~2,300 characters of plain text (fewer with accents or other alphabets). They are created at 1024 px for Save PNG and ~600 px for Copy image, so they stay sharp when printed.

⚡ Performance

Measured on the development PC (Windows 11):
Idle CPU (60 s) 0 ms
Idle memory 0.6 MB working set, 2.1 MB private
Idle threads 1
Kodo.exe / installer 1.3 MB / 2.6 MB

🔧 Build

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ x64 tools and Inno Setup 6 (winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup).

.\build.ps1

It downloads the pinned dependencies into .deps/ (Windows SDK, CMake, Ninja and ZXing-C++, all verified by hash), builds everything, runs the tests and writes the installer to dist/KodoSetup.exe.

.\build.ps1 -SkipTests and .\build.ps1 -SkipInstaller skip those steps.

📚 Dependencies

  • Windows Imaging Component — PNG images, built into Windows
  • Media Foundation — the camera, built into Windows
  • Interface Sounds by Kenney — the read sound (CC0)

repo.name: Leaf-Markdown
repo.description: Leaf Markdown — Simple Markdown Reader. Opens .md files beautifully rendered on Windows 10/11, like a PDF reader for Markdown.

releases.body_html:
First release of Leaf Markdown, a minimal Markdown viewer for Windows 10/11.

Downloads

  • LeafMarkdown-Setup-1.0.0.exe: installer (recommended). Per-user install, no admin rights needed. It adds Leaf Markdown to the Start menu and opens .md files with it.
  • LeafMarkdown.exe: portable version, no installation. Run LeafMarkdown.exe --register to associate it with .md files.

Requirements

  • Windows 10/11 x64 with the WebView2 Runtime (included with up-to-date Windows).
  • .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64). The installer warns you if it's missing.

apps.readmeHtml:
🍃 Leaf Markdown — Simple Markdown Reader

A minimal Markdown viewer for Windows 10/11, built with C# and WebView2.
It opens .md files and shows them beautifully rendered, like a PDF reader but for Markdown. No editing, no sidebars, no tabs.

🚀 Features

  • GitHub-style rendering: tables, task lists, footnotes, alerts (> [!NOTE]), images and syntax-highlighted code
  • Opens almost instantly and uses little memory
  • Follows the Windows light or dark theme, title bar included
  • Live reload: when the file is saved by another program the view updates and keeps your reading position
  • Open files by double-click, drag & drop, Ctrl+O or the command line (LeafMarkdown.exe "file.md")
  • Zoom with Ctrl + mouse wheel (Ctrl+0 resets it) and find in the document with Ctrl+F

releases.body_html:
First release of Obex Password Vault 🔐

  • 🗄️ Encrypted vault in one local file: AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2 with Windows' own cryptography. Search, copy usernames and passwords with one click; the clipboard clears itself after 30 seconds and stays out of Win + V

  • 📥 Import from Chrome or Edge, export to CSV, daily encrypted backups
  • ⏱️ Auto-lock after inactivity, when Windows locks or the PC sleeps
  • 🔒 100% offline: no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry

Install: download ObexSetup.exe below and run it. Per-user install, no admin rights needed. Windows 10 (1809+) and 11, 64-bit.

apps.readmeHtml:
🔐 Obex — Password Vault

Your passwords in one encrypted file, on your PC. 🗝️
Unlock it with Windows Hello, find any password in a second and copy it with one click. Press Ctrl + Alt + O anywhere for a new strong password, and keep it in your vault in the same step.

Obex (Latin for bolt or barrier) lives in the notification area and works 100% offline: no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

  

🚀 Features

  • ⚡ Quick password (Ctrl + Alt + O): a small panel pops up in the corner with a new password, its strength and length. Copy it, or type a name, website and username to save it in your vault (if Obex is locked, it asks Windows Hello and saves it right after)
  • 🗄️ Vault: name, website, username, password and notes for each entry
    • 🔍 Search as you type, across names, websites, usernames and notes
    • 📋 Copy the username or password with one click; the clipboard is cleared after 30 seconds
    • 🙈 Copied passwords stay out of the Windows clipboard history (Win + V) and the cloud clipboard
    • 🌐 Open the website in your browser (web links only)
  • 🔒 Strong encryption: AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 rounds), all with Windows' own cryptography (CNG). No third-party crypto code
  • 👆 Windows Hello: unlock with your PIN, fingerprint or face. The master password is asked after every restart and at least once a week (you choose how often)
  • 🆘 Recovery code: if you forget your master password, a one-time code gets you back in. Print it or save it as an emergency sheet
  • ⏱️ Auto-lock after 15 minutes without using Obex (adjustable), and whenever you lock Windows or the PC sleeps
  • 🎲 Password generator: 4 to 128 characters, choose the kinds of characters, avoid look-alikes (l 1 I O 0), several at once, with a strength meter and an estimate of how long it would take to crack
  • #️⃣ Hash tools: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 of any text or file (drag and drop), compare with an expected hash and check .sha256 files
  • 📥 Import the passwords you exported from Chrome or Edge, 📤 export them back to CSV
  • 💾 Daily backups of the encrypted vault, the last 5 days
  • 🌙 Clean Windows 11 look that follows your light or dark theme and accent color
  • 🪶 No .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed

📦 Install

Download ObexSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Per-user install, no admin rights needed
  • Obex opens right away to create your vault, and starts with Windows from then on

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes Obex, its startup entry and its settings. Your vault and its backups are kept, so reinstalling brings everything back.

🖱️ Usage

Action How
Quick password Ctrl + Alt + O; Enter copies it (and saves it if you typed a name), Esc closes
Open Obex Click the tray icon, or Open Obex in the quick panel
Search Just type; ↓ or Enter jumps to the list
Copy password Copy button, double-click the entry, or Ctrl + C in the list
Copy username Copy button, or Ctrl + B in the list
Lock now Lock button, Ctrl + L, or right-click the tray icon → Lock now
Settings ⚙️ button (when unlocked)
Exit Right-click the tray icon → Exit Obex

Closing the window with ✕ keeps Obex running in the notification area; the vault stays unlocked until auto-lock kicks in.

🆘 Recovery code

When you create the vault, Obex shows a recovery code like K7QM-2XRP-9WFD-… once. Print it or save it and keep it somewhere safe; Obex asks you to type part of it back to make sure.

  • Forgot your master password? On the lock screen click Forgot your master password?, type the code and choose a new password. You then get a new code; the old one stops working.
  • You can make a new code at any time in Settings → New recovery code.

⚠️ Anyone with your recovery code can open your vault. If you lose both your master password and the recovery code, nobody can recover your passwords, not even VitomDev.

📥 Import from Chrome or Edge

  1. In Chrome go to chrome://password-manager/settings (in Edge, edge://wallet/passwords) and export your passwords to a CSV file.
  2. In Obex: Settings → Import from Chrome or Edge… and pick the file. Entries already in your vault are skipped.
  3. Obex offers to delete the CSV afterwards: it holds your passwords in plain text.

💾 Backups

Obex keeps one copy per day of your encrypted vault, the last 5 days, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Obex Password Vault\Backups. Settings → Save a copy of the vault… saves one wherever you like (a USB stick, for example).

To restore a copy: exit Obex, copy the backup over %LOCALAPPDATA%\Obex Password Vault\vault.obex and start Obex again. It opens with the master password and recovery code that were valid when the copy was made.

🛡️ How it protects your data

  • A random 256-bit vault key encrypts all entries with AES-256-GCM, which also detects any change to the file.
  • That key is stored twice in the file, encrypted with a key derived from your master password and with one derived from your recovery code (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 rounds each). Your master password is never stored.
  • Windows Hello uses a key kept in your PC's security chip (TPM): Hello signs a fixed challenge and that signature unlocks a third copy of the vault key, stored for your Windows user only (DPAPI). It works only in the same Windows sign-in as your last master password and for a limited number of days.
  • Passwords are wiped from memory when Obex locks, and nothing ever leaves your PC.

🔧 Build

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ x64 tools and Inno Setup 6 (winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup).

.\build.ps1

It downloads the pinned build tools into .deps/ (Windows SDK, CMake and Ninja, all verified by hash), builds everything, runs the tests and writes the installer to dist/ObexSetup.exe.

.\build.ps1 -SkipTests and .\build.ps1 -SkipInstaller skip those steps.

📚 Dependencies

None beyond Windows itself: CNG (bcrypt.dll) for encryption and hashes, DPAPI and Windows Hello (KeyCredentialManager).

🪟 Compatibility

Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer) and Windows 11, 64-bit.

Move files between your PC and your phone over Wi-Fi. 📲💻

First release of Tono Audio Priority 🎧

  • 📋 Priority list: drag your audio outputs into order; the first one that is on becomes the default output
  • 🔌 Follows Bluetooth earbuds, USB headsets and monitors as Windows sees them come and go
  • 🎮 Wireless USB headsets that stay "connected" while off can be detected through HeadsetControl, downloaded only if you ask for it and verified by hash

apps.readmeHtml:
🎧 Tono — Audio Priority

Put your audio outputs in order and let Windows follow it. 🔊
Earbuds out of the case? Sound goes there. Headset on? It goes to the headset. Nothing else? The monitor. Tono always picks the first output on your list that is actually on.

Windows only switches when the output in use disappears, and then to whatever it likes. Tono lives in the notification area, does nothing until something connects or disconnects, and never fights you when you pick an output yourself. 🪶

🚀 Features

  • 📋 Priority list: drag your outputs into order; the first one that is on becomes the default
  • 🔌 Follows what Windows sees: Bluetooth earbuds going into their case, USB headsets unplugged, monitors turned off
  • 🎮 Wireless USB headsets that stay "connected" while switched off (Logitech, SteelSeries, HyperX, Corsair and many more): Tono can ask them directly through HeadsetControl, downloaded only if you want it
  • ✋ Manual mode for anything that cannot be detected: mark it on or off from the tray menu
  • 🧪 Test each output: turn it off and on while Tono watches, and it tells you how it can be detected
  • 🚫 Never use an output: switch it off in the list (handy for virtual devices)
  • 🙋 Your choice wins: if you, a game or SteamVR pick another output, Tono leaves it until the next device connects or disconnects
  • ⏸️ Pause from the panel or the tray menu
  • 💬 Small notifications next to the clock when Tono switches output, with the reason (JBL Tune Buds 2 is off), and when it pauses. They never take focus and stay away during full-screen games and Do not disturb
  • 🆕 New outputs are added at the end of the list and Tono tells you, so you can put them where you want
  • ⏳ Waits a moment before switching, so Bluetooth hiccups and monitors going to sleep do not make it jump around
  • 🛡️ When in doubt, it does nothing: if a headset does not answer, the output stays as it is
  • 🎤 Bluetooth "Hands-Free" duplicates are hidden; the good-quality stereo output is used
  • 🔒 100% offline: nothing leaves your PC. No telemetry, no accounts
  • 🌙 Clean Windows 11 look that follows your light or dark theme and accent color
  • 🪶 Tiny: ~0 CPU while idle, a ~0.4 MB program, no .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed
  • 🚦 Starts with Windows (you can turn it off)

📦 Install

Download TonoSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Per-user install, no admin rights needed
  • Tono starts right away and opens its list, starting with the output you are using now
  • It starts with Windows from then on

💡 Windows may put new icons in the hidden icons area (^). Drag Tono's icon onto the taskbar to always see it.

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes Tono, its startup entry, its settings and HeadsetControl if it was downloaded.

🖱️ Usage

Action How
Open the list Left-click the tray icon
Change the order Drag an output up or down
Never use an output Turn off its switch
Test an output ··· next to it → Test detection…
Choose how it is detected ··· next to it → Windows / HeadsetControl / manual
Mark a manual output on or off Right-click the tray icon → … is on
Pause ⏸️ in the panel, or right-click the tray icon → Pause switching
Also switch the communications output (calls, Discord) Right-click the tray icon → Also switch the communications output
Small notifications on or off Right-click the tray icon → Small notifications
Start with Windows Right-click the tray icon → Start with Windows
Exit Right-click the tray icon → Exit Tono

The tray icon turns grey while Tono is paused, and its tooltip shows the output in use.

🧪 Testing an output

Tono asks you to switch the output off, then on again, and watches:

  1. Windows noticed → Automatic. Nothing else needed (most Bluetooth earbuds and plugged-in headsets).
  2. Windows did not notice (common with wireless USB headsets, whose receiver stays plugged in) → Tono offers to download HeadsetControl, then tests again. If HeadsetControl can tell → HeadsetControl.
  3. Nobody noticed → Manual: mark it on or off yourself from the tray menu.

Monitors and virtual devices do not need a test.

🎮 About HeadsetControl

HeadsetControl is a free, open-source tool (GPL v3) by Denis Arnst and contributors that talks to many wireless headsets. It is not included in Tono. Only when you ask for it, Tono downloads version 4.2.0 from its official GitHub release, checks that the file is the genuine one (SHA-256) and runs it as a separate program every 3 seconds, only while an output on your list needs it. See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.

⚡ Performance

Tono does not poll Windows: it waits for Windows' own audio notifications and wakes up only when an output connects, disconnects or the default changes. The panel only exists while it is open.

Measured on the development PC (Windows 11, panel closed, over 30 s):
Idle 0 ms CPU
Tono.exe 0.43 MB

With a headset detected through HeadsetControl, Tono also starts HeadsetControl every 3 seconds (about 0.1 s each).

🔧 Build

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ x64 tools and Inno Setup 6 (winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup).

.\build.ps1

It downloads the pinned build tools into .deps/ (Windows SDK, CMake and Ninja, all verified by hash), builds everything, runs the tests and writes the installer to dist/TonoSetup.exe.

.\build.ps1 -SkipTests and .\build.ps1 -SkipInstaller skip those steps.

📚 Dependencies

None: Tono only uses Windows' own APIs (Core Audio notifications, IPolicyConfig to set the default output, the same one Windows' sound settings use). HeadsetControl is optional and never bundled. 🧘

🪟 Compatibility

Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer) and Windows 11, 64-bit.

apps.readmeHtml:
📊 Vela — System Monitor

Keep an eye on your PC without opening Task Manager. 👀
CPU and memory live in the tray icon, a tooltip sums up everything, and one click opens a small panel with CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and battery. Want the numbers always in sight? Turn on the floating widget or show them right on the taskbar.

Vela lives in the notification area and is built to stay out of the way: a monitor that eats your resources would defeat its own purpose. 🪶



🚀 Features

  • 📈 Tray icon: the Vela logo, or the live CPU or memory percent as a number
  • 💬 Tooltip: hover the icon for CPU, RAM, disk, network speed and battery at a glance
  • 🪟 Panel: click the icon for a Windows 11–style flyout with every metric and its level bar
  • 📉 History graphs: CPU, GPU, memory and network draw their recent past right in the panel
  • 🔎 Top processes: click CPU, GPU, Memory or Disk in the panel to see the 10 apps using the most of it, updated every second
  • 🛑 End a process or find its file: right-click it in a top list
  • 🚨 High usage warnings (optional): a notification when CPU, GPU or memory stay at 90% or more; click it to see what is using it
  • 📌 Floating widget: a tiny always-on-top box with CPU, RAM and network speed. Drag it anywhere, it remembers where
  • 🧷 On the taskbar: the same numbers blended into your taskbar, next to the clock, at the left or anywhere you drag them
  • 🎛️ Show only what you care about: pick which metrics appear in the panel, and which on the taskbar and floating widget
  • 🧠 CPU: total usage, logical processors and uptime
  • 🎮 GPU: usage, as Task Manager measures it, and video memory
  • 🧮 Memory: used and total RAM
  • 💽 Disk: space used on the system drive plus live read and write speed
  • 🌐 Network: download and upload speed of your physical adapters (Wi-Fi, Ethernet)
  • 🔋 Battery: charge, charging state and time left (only on devices with a battery)
  • 🚨 Values at 90% or more turn red, in the panel and in the tray icon
  • 😴 Stops sampling while the screen is off
  • 🔒 100% offline: nothing leaves your PC. No telemetry, no accounts
  • 🌙 Clean Windows 11 look that follows your light or dark theme and accent color
  • 🪶 Tiny: ~1.3 MB of memory and ~0.03% CPU while running, a ~2.1 MB installer, no .NET or Visual C++ runtime needed
  • 🚦 Starts with Windows (you can turn it off)

📦 Install

Download VelaSetup.exe from Releases and run it.

🧰 Recommended: install it with Vitool Box, which keeps all VitomDev apps in one place and installs or removes them with a switch.

  • Per-user install, no admin rights needed
  • Vela starts right away and its icon appears in the notification area
  • It starts with Windows from then on

💡 Windows may put new icons in the hidden icons area (^). Drag Vela's icon onto the taskbar to always see it.

Uninstalling (Settings → Apps) removes Vela, its startup entry and its settings.

🖱️ Usage

Action How
Quick look Hover the tray icon
Open the panel Left-click the tray icon
Close the panel Click anywhere else, or Esc
Top 10 processes Click CPU, GPU, Memory or Disk in the panel; click the title, Esc or Backspace to go back
End a process or open its folder Right-click it in a top list
Floating widget Right-click the tray icon → Floating widget. Drag to move, double-click for the panel, right-click for the menu
Numbers on the taskbar Right-click the tray icon → Show on taskbar. Click them for the panel, drag them along the taskbar to move them, right-click for the menu
Settings ⚙️ in the panel, or right-click the tray icon → Settings
Start with Windows Right-click the tray icon → Start with Windows
Exit Right-click the tray icon → Exit Vela

⚙️ Settings

  • Tray icon shows: Vela logo, CPU % or memory %
  • What to show: CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network and battery, chosen separately for the panel and for the taskbar and floating widget
  • Floating widget above other windows, on or off
  • Show on the taskbar, on or off, and its position: next to the clock or at the left (dragging it there works too)
  • Taskbar on screens: with more than one screen, choose which taskbars show it (one, several or all)
  • Update: every 1, 2 (default) or 5 seconds. The panel always updates every second while it is open
  • Start with Windows
  • History graphs in the panel: on by default; off shows plain bars
  • Warn when CPU, GPU or memory stay at 90%: off by default. A warning comes after 30 seconds at 90% or more, and the same one only comes back once usage has dropped and 10 minutes have passed

⚡ Performance

Vela reads the system counters every 2 seconds and only redraws the tray icon or a panel row when what you would see actually changes. The panel only exists while it is open, and processes are only read while it is open: one system call per second for all of them, with no handle opened to any process. The GPU is read from the same counters Task Manager uses, which cost more, so only while the panel, the taskbar, the widget or the warnings need it.

Measured on the development PC (Windows 11, default settings, panel closed, over 60 s):
Tray only 16 ms CPU (~0.03%), 1.3–1.8 MB working set
With floating widget and taskbar view 31 ms CPU (~0.05%), 2.5 MB working set
Taskbar view showing the GPU 94 ms CPU (~0.16%), 9.9 MB working set
Vela.exe / installer 0.24 MB / 2.1 MB

🔧 Build

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ x64 tools and Inno Setup 6 (winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup).

.\build.ps1

It downloads the pinned build tools into .deps/ (Windows SDK, CMake and Ninja, all verified by hash), builds everything, runs the tests and writes the installer to dist/VelaSetup.exe.

.\build.ps1 -SkipTests and .\build.ps1 -SkipInstaller skip those steps.

📚 Dependencies

None: Vela only uses Windows' own APIs (GetSystemTimes, GlobalMemoryStatusEx, GetIfEntry2, GetSystemPowerStatus, disk performance counters, and the GPU counters through PDH and DXGI). 🧘

🪟 Compatibility

Windows 10 (version 1809 or newer) and Windows 11, 64-bit.

🧪 Project Status

✅ Stable.
This project is fully functional as-is and ready to use. Future updates to improve features or the interface are not ruled out.
